title: Месть по старинному рецепту  (Revenge by an Old Recipe)

segments.t: Unaware that the new salad order is actually for Nagiyev, Chef Barinov and his cooks gleefully concoct a revolting plate using every foul ingredient in reach. Minutes after sending it out, a furious Nagiyev bursts into the kitchen demanding to know who made the garbage he just ate.
И последний штрих.
Это что?
Но на вкус пальчики оближут.
Так что давай, неси.
Это старинный французский рецепт.
Так, красавцы.
Какая тебе разница?
Посмотри, что это вы приготовили мне, а?
Что это за гадость, я вас спрашиваю, а?
Дим, ну мы не знали, что это тебе.
Что за бардак на кухне, а?
Какая разница кому?
Вы устроили?

'And now for the finishing touch.' The meaning hinges on 'both' working together with 'stroke' in spoken Russian.

'What on earth is that?' Chef Viktor anchors the line on 'this', while 'what' completes the thought.
Но на вкус пальчики оближут.
'They will lick their fingers from the taste.' Dmitry anchors the line on 'but', while 'to lick' completes the thought. Chef Viktor answers right away.
Так что давай, неси.
'So go on, carry it out.' In Russian, the idea of 'like this' flows naturally into 'bring' without extra filler words.
Это старинный французский рецепт.
'It is an ancient French recipe.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'this' before landing on 'recipe'.
Так, красавцы.
'Alright, you beauties.' The grammar packs 'like this' and 'handsome man' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Dmitry answers right away.
Какая тебе разница?
'What difference does it make to you?' Dmitry raises the pitch on 'difference' to turn the phrase into a direct spoken question.
Посмотри, что это вы приготовили мне, а?
'Take a look at what you just cooked for me, huh?' The meaning hinges on 'look' working together with 'and' in spoken Russian.
Что это за гадость, я вас спрашиваю, а?
'What is this filth, I am asking all of you!' The meaning hinges on 'what' working together with 'and' in spoken Russian. Chef Viktor answers right away.
Дим, ну мы не знали, что это тебе.
'Dima, we had no idea that plate was for you.' The grammar packs 'Dima' and 'you' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Что за бардак на кухне, а?
'What kind of chaos is going on in this kitchen?' Dmitry anchors the line on 'what', while 'and' completes the thought.
Какая разница кому?
'What difference does it make who it was for?' Chef Viktor raises the pitch on 'to whom' to turn the phrase into a direct spoken question. Dmitry answers right away.
Вы устроили?
